title: Silas and the Harvest
premise: Silas Marsh, a scholarship student at Hollowbrook Academy, notices classmates vanishing from photographs and then from memory itself, while the new teacher, Ivo Voss, seems to be counting doors and keeping lights on for reasons of his own. Following clues to her grandmother's house—where every family photo now includes an extra empty chair—Silas learns she is descended from the school's founders, who bound a hungry harvest entity beneath the grounds with an unfinished ritual. As the harvest moon rises, Ivo reveals he is the last loyal warden trying to complete it, but completing the ritual demands a founder's blood: Silas must choose between belonging to a town that erased her family and telling the truth that will break the cycle. In the end, Silas finishes the ritual with her own blood freely given, unbinding the founders' corruption rather than feeding it, and the missing students return—though one chair remains in every photograph, waiting.
about_author: Rosalind Almeida is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent a decade collecting local legends about founding families and their debts. She writes horror about institutions that remember more than the people inside them.

chapters.title: The Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Silas arrives at Hollowbrook Academy on scholarship, immediately an outsider among legacy students. She observes Ivo Voss, the new teacher, methodically counting doors each evening and keeping classroom lights burning. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: wary curiosity—the sense of rules no one has explained.

chapters.title: Attendance Is a Kindness
chapters.summary: A classmate, Wren, stops appearing—not expelled, not transferred; teachers simply skip her name. When Silas asks, everyone insists Wren never existed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: gaslit unease deepening into quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Visiting her grandmother's house for the holiday, Silas finds old family photographs now contain an unfamiliar empty chair beside her ancestors. Her grandmother refuses to discuss the founders or the school. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread rooted in family silence.

chapters.title: What the Lights Keep Out
chapters.summary: Back at school, Silas follows Ivo after dark and sees him replacing bulbs along a corridor that shouldn't have fixtures. He catches her watching and warns her, not unkindly, to be invisible. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the first hint that Ivo is protecting, not menacing.

chapters.title: The Founders' Portraits
chapters.summary: Researching in the library, Silas discovers portraits of four founders—one face scratched out—and a ledger listing 'harvest tithes' dated every nineteen years. This year falls due. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: intellectual thrill curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Wren's Locker
chapters.summary: Silas finds Wren's untouched locker containing a note: 'It takes whoever remembers you least.' Silas realizes remembering the missing may mark her next. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: guilt and terror entwined—her loyalty to Wren is now a liability.

chapters.title: Ivo's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Ivo admits he is a warden, heir to a line sworn to maintain the founders' binding. The ritual was left unfinished by cowardice generations ago; each harvest, the entity takes a payment instead. POV: alternating Silas/Ivo. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance formed over shared secrets.

chapters.title: The Chair Moves Closer
chapters.summary: In grandmother's newest photos, the extra chair has moved nearer the family group. Grandmother finally whispers that the Marshes were founders—and that the scratched-out portrait is her own mother. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: inheritance as curse; belonging revealed as bait.

chapters.title: Nineteen Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ivo recounts the last harvest: his predecessor chose a scapegoat student to satisfy the entity and preserve the town. Ivo refused to repeat it and has been stretching the binding with light and counted thresholds ever since. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: weariness of a man complicit in delay, not salvation.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets
chapters.summary: Silas canvases townsfolk about the missing students and meets warm smiles and blank eyes. The whole community is complicit in forgetting—a belonging purchased with erasure. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening her resolve toward truth.

chapters.title: Marks on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Chalk sigils appear on Silas's dormitory door overnight. Ivo identifies them as the entity learning her name; being remembered by it means being claimed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: hunted; invisibility is no longer possible.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Following the founders' ledger, Silas and Ivo find a sealed undercroft beneath the chapel: a stone table, four founder marks, and a fifth carved fresh. The ritual requires all five lines of blood. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion at the machinery of the bargain.

chapters.title: A Debt in the Family
chapters.summary: Grandmother gives Silas the founders' original covenant and confesses her mother fled mid-ritual, leaving the binding incomplete—that flight is why the chair appears unfinished in every photograph. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief for an ancestor's cowardice, and fury at inherited duty.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Bargain
chapters.summary: The headmaster, himself a descendant of a founder line, offers Silas protection if she names another student as tithe—an echo of the old sin. She refuses. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation of safety versus integrity; power's corruption made personal.

chapters.title: Lights Failing
chapters.summary: Bulbs burst across campus in a spreading wave; doors Ivo counted stand open where none were. The entity is testing the boundaries. A first-year goes missing that night. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: a warden's guilt as his safeguards fail one by one.

chapters.title: What Remembers You
chapters.summary: Silas dreams of the undercroft and wakes with chalk on her own palms—she has been walking in her sleep, answering the summons. Ivo tells her the claiming has begun. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: loss of control; the horror is now inside her.

chapters.title: Three Lines Gathered
chapters.summary: Ivo secures blood consent from two other founder descendants—one eagerly, hoping for favor; one brokenly. The headmaster withholds his, demanding the tithe alternative. Loyalties fracture. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the ritual's arithmetic of coercion exposed.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: The moon swells red. Missing students appear at windows, present but hollow-eyed, held as collateral. Silas understands: finishing the ritual as designed would free them only into a new servitude. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: clarity—the founders' ritual itself is the corruption.

chapters.title: The Fifth Line
chapters.summary: In the undercroft, the headmaster attempts to force Silas's blood as the final line; Ivo turns against him, choosing truth over the institution he served. The entity rises through the floor as the moon crests. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: betrayal and sacrifice colliding at the threshold.

chapters.title: Silas and the Harvest
chapters.summary: Rather than complete the binding, Silas speaks the covenant's hidden clause—blood given, not taken—and offers hers freely, unmaking the founders' bargain. The entity, fed by coercion for centuries, dissolves in the honest gift. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax; agency reclaimed through truth.

chapters.title: The Returning
chapters.summary: Dawn. The missing students wake in the dormitories with full memories; the town begins recalling what it paid to forget. The headmaster is gone—taken by the debt he tried to spend others against. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: bittersweet restoration; justice incomplete but real.

chapters.title: One Chair Remains
chapters.summary: Weeks later, new photographs show the family whole—but in grandmother's house, one empty chair still stands by the window, and sometimes, at dusk, it is warm. Silas keeps the lights on. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: resolution with a resonant scar—belonging earned, vigilance kept.
